functions.name: mlk_poly_add
functions.role: In-place polynomial addition over coefficient arrays; updates the first operand accumulator `r` by adding corresponding coefficients from `b`.
outputs: No return value; mutates r->coeffs in place
preconditions_or_contracts: `r` and `b` must be memory-no-alias fresh objects per `memory_no_alias(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))` and `memory_no_alias(b, sizeof(mlk_poly))`.
For every coefficient index `k0` in [0, MLKEM_N), `(int32_t) r->coeffs[k0] + b->coeffs[k0] <= INT16_MAX`.
For every coefficient index `k1` in [0, MLKEM_N), `(int32_t) r->coeffs[k1] + b->coeffs[k1] >= INT16_MIN`.
postconditions_or_contracts: For every coefficient index `k` in [0, MLKEM_N), `r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k]`.
`assigns(memory_slice(r, sizeof(mlk_poly)))` limits writes to the `r` object.

evidence_references.locator: Function `mlk_poly_add`, lines in body and surrounding comment
evidence_references.excerpt: /* Reference: `poly_add()` in the reference implementation @[REF]. *            - We use destructive version (output=first input) to avoid *              reasoning about aliasing in the CBMC specification */ ... void mlk_poly_add(mlk_poly *r, const mlk_poly *b) { ... invariant(forall(k0, i, MLKEM_N, r->coeffs[k0] == loop_entry(*r).coeffs[k0])) ... invariant(forall(k1, 0, i, r->coeffs[k1] == loop_entry(*r).coeffs[k1] + b->coeffs[k1])) ... r->coeffs[i] = (int16_t)(r->coeffs[i] + b->coeffs[i]); }
evidence_references.supports_claim: Function is in-place, updates r by coefficient-wise integer addition, and uses loop invariants expressing old-state/new-state relation.

evidence_references.excerpt: /* Add two polynomials in place. ... The coefficients of @p r and @p b must be such that the addition does not overflow. Otherwise, the behaviour of this function is undefined. ... @param[in,out] r Input-output polynomial to be added to. @param[in]     b Input polynomial that should be added to @p r. Must be disjoint from @p r. */ ... requires(memory_no_alias(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(memory_no_alias(b, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(forall(k0, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k0] + b->coeffs[k0] <= INT16_MAX)) requires(forall(k1, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k1] + b->coeffs[k1] >= INT16_MIN)) ensures(forall(k, 0, MLKEM_N, r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k])) assigns(memory_slice(r, sizeof(mlk_poly)))
evidence_references.supports_claim: The public contract explicitly states in-place addition, disjoint inputs, overflow-preventing preconditions, and old/new-state postcondition.

evidence_references.excerpt: @spec{@[FIPS203, 2.4.5, Arithmetic With Polynomials and NTT Representations]. Used in @[FIPS203, Algorithm 14 (K-PKE.Encrypt), L21].}
evidence_references.supports_claim: Implementation comment links the routine to the FIPS arithmetic-with-polynomials section and K-PKE.Encrypt line 21 as a likely use site.

functions.uncertainty: The code and contract are explicit about exact integer addition semantics in `int16_t` and about no modular reduction. The broader FIPS semantics are coordinate-wise modulo-q addition, but this function’s C-level contract is the overflow-free accumulator form, not an explicit modular-add routine.
limitations: This stage does not prove the function is fully correct for all uses; it only records observed code and contract facts.
The implementation comment says it is a reference-implementation counterpart and cites FIPS 203 section 2.4.5, but the function itself is specialized to destructive accumulator semantics.
No separate source file beyond `poly.c`, `poly.h`, `params.h`, `cbmc.h`, and the provided FIPS text was available for this stage.
The function `mlk_poly_add` does not perform modular reduction; downstream property work should not assume canonical representative normalization from this routine alone.

functions.name: mlk_poly_sub
functions.role: In-place polynomial subtraction routine on coefficient arrays; included because the configured property family covers polynomial addition/subtraction bounds and the source places add/sub side by side.
outputs: No return value; mutates r->coeffs in place
preconditions_or_contracts: `r` and `b` must be memory-no-alias fresh objects.
For every coefficient index `k0`, `(int32_t) r->coeffs[k0] - b->coeffs[k0] <= INT16_MAX`.
For every coefficient index `k1`, `(int32_t) r->coeffs[k1] - b->coeffs[k1] >= INT16_MIN`.
postconditions_or_contracts: For every coefficient index `k`, `r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] - b->coeffs[k]`.
`assigns(memory_slice(r, sizeof(mlk_poly)))` limits writes to the `r` object.

evidence_references.excerpt: void mlk_poly_sub(mlk_poly *r, const mlk_poly *b) { ... invariant(forall(k1, 0, i, r->coeffs[k1] == loop_entry(*r).coeffs[k1] - b->coeffs[k1])) ... r->coeffs[i] = (int16_t)(r->coeffs[i] - b->coeffs[i]); }
evidence_references.supports_claim: Parallel in-place subtraction routine and its loop invariant/post-state relation.

evidence_references.excerpt: /* Subtract two polynomials; no modular reduction is performed. ... requires(memory_no_alias(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(memory_no_alias(b, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(forall(k0, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k0] - b->coeffs[k0] <= INT16_MAX)) requires(forall(k1, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k1] - b->coeffs[k1] >= INT16_MIN)) ensures(forall(k, 0, MLKEM_N, r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] - b->coeffs[k])) assigns(memory_slice(r, sizeof(mlk_poly)))
evidence_references.supports_claim: Explicit subtraction contract and no-modular-reduction statement.
